title: Care Team Leads, Caseloads and Program Model across Care Management Tiers
content:
Every Care Management tier names the role that leads the member's care team, the most members that one lead carries, whether the tier is delivered only through digital coaching, whether remote monitoring devices may be supplied, and how many member-requested changes of care team lead the tier allows within a rolling 365 days.

## Staffing standard by tier

| Care Management tier | Care team lead | Most members per lead (caseload) | Delivered only through digital coaching | Remote monitoring devices may be supplied | Member-requested lead changes within a rolling 365 days |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Healthy Living Support | Digital health coach | 0 | Yes | No | 0 |
| Care Coordination Level 1 | Nurse care coordinator | 150 | No | No | 1 |
| Care Coordination Level 2 | Nurse care coordinator | 90 | No | Yes | 1 |
| Maternal Care Management | Maternal nurse | 60 | No | Yes | 1 |
| Complex Case Management | Nurse case manager | 45 | No | Yes | 2 |
| Health Home Services | Health Home care coordinator | 60 | No | Yes | 2 |
| LTSS Service Coordination | LTSS service coordinator | 50 | No | No | 2 |

## Notes on the columns

- **Care team lead** is the role that leads the member's care team in that tier. Care Coordination Level 1 and Level 2 share the same lead role, the nurse care coordinator, but at different caseloads (150 and 90).
- **Caseload** is the most members one care team lead carries, counted in members.
- **Digital coaching only**: Healthy Living Support is the one tier delivered only through digital coaching; every other tier is not limited to digital coaching.
- **Remote monitoring**: devices may be supplied in Care Coordination Level 2, Maternal Care Management, Complex Case Management and Health Home Services, and not in Healthy Living Support, Care Coordination Level 1 or LTSS Service Coordination.
- **Lead changes** counts changes of care team lead that the member asks for within a rolling 365 days: 0 in Healthy Living Support, 1 in Care Coordination Level 1, Level 2 and Maternal Care Management, and 2 in Complex Case Management, Health Home Services and LTSS Service Coordination.

## Comparing two tiers (hypothetical)

A member who moves from Care Coordination Level 2 to Complex Case Management moves from a nurse care coordinator carrying at most 90 members to a nurse case manager carrying at most 45, and from 1 to 2 member-requested lead changes in a rolling 365 days; remote monitoring devices may be supplied in both tiers.
